Worms Synagogue.event: The first synagogue was founded in the medieval Jewish quarter of Worms.

Old New Synagogue.event: The Gothic synagogue was completed in Prague's Jewish quarter.

Remuh Synagogue.event: The present masonry synagogue was completed in Kazimierz.
Postwar restoration returned the building to religious use.

Ibn Danan Synagogue.event: The synagogue was established in the Jewish quarter of Fez during the seventeenth century; the mapped year is approximate.

Great Synagogue of Vilna.event: The monumental synagogue was built after permission was granted for a stone structure.
The synagogue was looted and badly damaged during the German occupation.
Soviet authorities completed demolition of the ruined synagogue complex.

Portuguese Synagogue of Amsterdam.event: The Esnoga was inaugurated on its present site beside the Waterlooplein district.

Hurva Synagogue.event: The first Ashkenazi synagogue was founded on the site.
Creditors destroyed the unfinished synagogue and courtyard.
A large domed synagogue was dedicated on the recovered site.
The building was destroyed during the battle for the Jewish Quarter.
The reconstructed synagogue was dedicated and returned to regular use.

Great Synagogue of Gibraltar.event: Sha'ar Hashamayim was founded on Engineer Lane in Gibraltar.

Board of Deputies of British Jews.event: Delegates from London's Sephardi and Ashkenazi congregations formed representative committees that developed into the Board of Deputies.
The Board's registered office was at ORT House, 147 Arlington Road, London.

Touro Synagogue.event: The synagogue was dedicated for Newport's Sephardic congregation.
The building was designated a National Historic Site.

Mir Yeshiva.event: World War II outbreak; yeshiva fled eastward.
Entire yeshiva arrived in Shanghai, China, where it remained through the war.
Reestablished in Jerusalem by Rabbi Eliezer Yehuda Finkel.
Branch established in Brooklyn, New York.

Etz Chaim Yeshiva.event: The Talmud Torah and yeshiva were founded in Jerusalem's Old City.
The institution moved into its Jaffa Road complex.

B'nai B'rith International.event: Twelve German-Jewish immigrants founded B'nai B'rith on New York's Lower East Side.
The international headquarters moved to Washington, D.C.

Dohány Street Synagogue.event: The Great Synagogue was consecrated in Pest.
The synagogue stood within the Budapest ghetto during the Holocaust.
A major post-Communist restoration was completed.

Alliance Israélite Universelle.event: The Alliance Israélite Universelle was founded in Paris.
Its headquarters operated at 27 avenue de Ségur in Paris.

Kelm Talmud Torah Yeshiva.event: Rabbi Simcha Zissel Ziv appointed head and transformed the Talmud Torah into a Musar-oriented yeshiva.
Permanent campus purchased and new building constructed.
Exiled to Grobin, Courland (now Latvia), where Rabbi Ziv reestablished the yeshiva temporarily.
Returned to Kelm; developed into a central Musar yeshiva.
Death of Rabbi Simcha Zissel Ziv; succession by his brother Rabbi Aryeh Leib Broida, later his son-in-law Rabbi Tzvi Hirsch Broida and Rabbi Nachum Ze’ev Ziv.
Leadership passed to Rabbi Reuven Dov Dessler and then to Rabbis Daniel Movshovitz and Gershon Miadnik.
On June 21, 1941, Lithuanian collaborators and the Gestapo murdered the students and townspeople; the yeshiva was destroyed.

New Synagogue, Berlin.event: The New Synagogue was inaugurated at Oranienburger Strasse 29–31.

Spanish Synagogue of Prague.event: The new Moorish Revival synagogue opened in Prague.
The restored building reopened as a synagogue and museum venue.

Radun Yeshiva.event: Founded in Radun, Belarus by the Chofetz Chaim.
Disrupted during World War I; students scattered.
Yeshiva rebuilt after the war; continued under Rabbi Naftoli Trop.
Destroyed during the Holocaust; students and faculty murdered.

United Synagogue.event: Five London congregations united under the office of the Chief Rabbi to form the United Synagogue.
The organisation's principal offices operated at 305 Ballards Lane, North Finchley.

Central Synagogue.event: The Lexington Avenue synagogue building was completed.
A major fire severely damaged the sanctuary.

Hildesheimer Rabbinical Seminary.event: The seminary opened in Berlin; the marker identifies its historic institutional setting rather than a surviving campus entrance.

Princes Road Synagogue.event: The synagogue was consecrated on Princes Road in Liverpool.

Hebrew Union College.event: Hebrew Union College was founded in Cincinnati.
The Cincinnati campus moved to its present Clifton Avenue setting.

Telz Yeshiva.event: Flourished under Rabbi Eliezer Gordon and Rabbi Yosef Leib Bloch.
Reestablished in Cleveland, Ohio by survivors.

Great Synagogue of Florence.event: The Great Synagogue was completed on Via Luigi Carlo Farini in Florence.

Slabodka Yeshiva.event: Founded in Slabodka, Lithuania, under Rabbi Nosson Tzvi Finkel.
Branch established in Hebron, Mandatory Palestine.
Hebron massacre; yeshiva moved temporarily to Jerusalem.
Lithuanian yeshiva destroyed in the Holocaust.
Hebron branch reestablished permanently in Bnei Brak, Israel.

Lomza Yeshiva.event: The yeshiva was founded in Łomża.
A permanent branch opened in Petah Tikva.
The original Polish yeshiva was destroyed during the Holocaust; the Petah Tikva branch continued.

Jewish Theological Seminary.event: The seminary was founded in New York City.
Its principal complex opened at 3080 Broadway in Morningside Heights.

Yeshiva University and RIETS.event: Etz Chaim Yeshiva was founded on Manhattan's Lower East Side.
The Rabbi Isaac Elchanan Theological Seminary was established.
The institution moved to its Washington Heights campus.
The institution formally became Yeshiva University.

Eldridge Street Synagogue.event: The synagogue opened at 12 Eldridge Street on Manhattan's Lower East Side.

National Library of Israel.event: The Abarbanel Library, a principal institutional ancestor of the National Library, was founded in Jerusalem.
The library moved to the Lady Davis Building on the Hebrew University Givat Ram campus.
The new National Library building opened opposite the Knesset in Jerusalem.

Novardok Yeshiva.event: Founded by Rabbi Yosef Yozel Horwitz.
The size of the Yeshivah reaches 200 pupils.
After the Bolshevik takeover of Russia, the Alter sends his students across to Poland in secrecy. Many were shot or sent to Siberia for doing so. 600 made it.
THe Yeshiva goes to Kiev fleeing the war. There is a typhus outbreak where the Alter passes away.

Mesivta Rabsa Eitz Chaim D'Slutsk (Sluts.event: Founded in Slutsk by Rabbi Yaakov Dovid Willovsky (Ridvaz), who invited top students from Slabodka Yeshiva; Rabbi Isser Zalman Meltzer appointed rosh yeshiva.
Rabbi Aharon Kotler led 50 students to escape Soviet Russia and reestablish the yeshiva in Kletsk, Poland.
New yeshiva building dedicated in Kletsk with thousands attending; Rabbi Meltzer traveled from Palestine to participate.
Yeshiva escaped to Lithuania; regrouped in Jonava near Kaunas under Rabbi Aharon Kotler, with ~150 students.
In 1940, the Soviets annexed Lithuania, and afraid, the yeshiva divided into three groups (to make it harder to destroy the entire yeshiva).

World Zionist Organization.event: The First Zionist Congress established the Zionist Organization in Basel.
The national institutions developed their permanent centre in the Jewish Agency building on King George Street, Jerusalem.

Orthodox Union.event: The Union of Orthodox Jewish Congregations of America was founded in New York City.
The OU established its headquarters at 40 Rector Street in Lower Manhattan.

Jewish National Fund.event: The Fifth Zionist Congress in Basel resolved to establish the Jewish National Fund.
The organisation entered the national-institutions complex on King George Street in Jerusalem.

World Mizrachi.event: Mizrachi was founded at a conference in Vilna.
World Mizrachi's Jerusalem centre operated on King George Street.

Great Synagogue of Rome.event: The new Great Synagogue was completed beside the Tiber.
A terrorist attack outside the synagogue killed a child and wounded many worshippers.

Yeshiva Rabbi Chaim Berlin.event: The yeshiva was founded in Brooklyn.
The yeshiva established its enduring campus on Coney Island Avenue in Brooklyn.

American Jewish Committee.event: The American Jewish Committee was founded in New York City.
AJC's global headquarters operated at 165 East 56th Street in Manhattan.

Yeshiva Ohel Torah-Baranovich.event: Founded in Baranovich by Rabbi Yosef Yoizel Horowitz, the Alter of Novardok, as part of the expanding Novardok yeshiva network.
The yeshiva developed into an important center of Mussar and Lithuanian-style Torah learning, attracting students from across the Russian Empire.
World War I forced the temporary closure and dispersal of the yeshiva.
Rabbi Elchonon Wasserman, a leading disciple of the Chofetz Chaim, became rosh yeshiva after encouragement from the Chofetz Chaim.
Under Rabbi Elchonon Wasserman, the yeshiva became internationally renowned for its clarity in Gemara learning and high academic standards.
The yeshiva reached several hundred students and became one of the major Torah centers in interwar Poland.
With the outbreak of World War II and the Soviet invasion of eastern Poland, the yeshiva faced severe disruption and uncertainty. They relocated to Vilnius on the advice of R'Chaim Ozer Grodzensky.
Rabbi Elchonon Wasserman relocated the Yeshivah to Semeliskes after the Red Army invaded and occupied Lithuania.
Rabbi Elchonon Wasserman and many תלמידים were murdered by Nazi collaborators in Kovno during the Holocaust, bringing the yeshiva to an end.

Ponevezh Yeshiva.event: The yeshiva was founded in Panevėžys, Lithuania.
The yeshiva was re-established in Bnei Brak.

Hadassah.event: Hadassah was founded at Temple Emanu-El in New York City.
Hadassah opened its major university hospital complex on Mount Scopus in Jerusalem.

World Agudath Israel.event: World Agudath Israel was founded at a conference in Katowice.
The movement maintained its principal Israeli offices in central Jerusalem.

American Jewish Joint Distribution Commi.event: American Jewish relief committees combined their overseas work through the Joint Distribution Committee in New York.
JDC's headquarters operated at 220 East 42nd Street in Manhattan.

Hebrew University of Jerusalem.event: The foundation stones of the Hebrew University were laid on Mount Scopus.
The university's Mount Scopus campus formally opened.
The Givat Ram campus opened after Mount Scopus had become inaccessible.

Porat Yosef Yeshiva.event: The Old City campus was inaugurated beside the Western Wall quarter.
The Old City building was destroyed during the battle for Jerusalem.
The Geula campus became the institution's principal postwar home.
A rebuilt Old City campus was dedicated.

Mercaz HaRav Yeshiva.event: The Central Universal Yeshiva was founded in Jerusalem.
The yeshiva moved to its Kiryat Moshe campus.
Eight students were murdered in a terrorist attack inside the yeshiva library.

Kamenitz Yeshiva.event: Founded in Kamenets-Litovsk by Rabbi Baruch Ber Leibowitz.
Became known as a premier Lithuanian yeshiva.

Gateshead Talmudical College.event: The yeshiva was founded in Gateshead.
Expansion around Bewick and Rectory Roads created the modern campus.

Jewish Agency for Israel.event: The enlarged Jewish Agency was formally constituted at Zurich.
Its Jerusalem headquarters opened in the national-institutions building on King George Street.

Chachmei Lublin Yeshiva.event: Founded by Rabbi Meir Shapiro in Lublin, Poland.

Ner Israel Rabbinical College.event: Ner Israel was founded in Baltimore.
The yeshiva moved to its Mount Wilson Lane campus in Pikesville.

World Jewish Congress.event: Delegates established the World Jewish Congress in Geneva.
The organisation's principal headquarters operated in New York City.

770 Eastern Parkway.event: Chabad-Lubavitch acquired 770 Eastern Parkway in Crown Heights as the residence and institutional centre of ר׳ יוסף יצחק שניאורסון.

Brisk Yeshiva, Jerusalem.event: The Brisker yeshiva tradition was re-established in Jerusalem.
Leadership passed to the next generation of the Brisk rabbinic family.

Beth Medrash Govoha.event: Beth Medrash Govoha opened in Lakewood, New Jersey.
The yeshiva expanded beyond its original study-hall building.

Yad Vashem.event: The Knesset established Yad Vashem as the Holocaust Martyrs' and Heroes' Remembrance Authority.
The new Holocaust History Museum opened on the Mount of Remembrance campus.

Kerem B'Yavneh.event: The yeshiva was founded beside Kvutzat Yavne and became the model for the hesder framework.

Bar-Ilan University.event: Bar-Ilan University opened its campus at Ramat Gan.

Yeshivat Sha'alvim.event: Yeshivat Sha'alvim was established at Kibbutz Sha'alvim.

Yeshivat HaKotel.event: The yeshiva was founded in Jerusalem's restored Jewish Quarter.
Its permanent building overlooking the Western Wall area was completed.

Yeshivat Har Etzion.event: The yeshiva began at Kfar Etzion.
The yeshiva moved to its permanent campus in Alon Shvut.

Ohr Somayach, Jerusalem.event: The institution was founded in Jerusalem.
It adopted the name Ohr Somayach and developed its principal Jerusalem campus on Shimon Hatzadik Street.

Aish HaTorah.event: Aish HaTorah was founded in Jerusalem.
Its expanded world centre opened opposite the Western Wall plaza in Jerusalem's Old City.

Simon Wiesenthal Center.event: The Simon Wiesenthal Center was founded in Los Angeles.
The associated Museum of Tolerance opened on West Pico Boulevard.

Belz Great Synagogue.event: The Great Synagogue was dedicated in northern Jerusalem as the world centre of Belz Hasidism.

Ohel Jakob Synagogue, Munich.event: The synagogue was dedicated at Sankt-Jakobs-Platz in central Munich.

Ben Ezra Synagogue.event: A synagogue was established on the Old Cairo site.
The building was extensively reconstructed while preserving the historic site.
The restored synagogue reopened following a major conservation project.
